title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is the reduction step in a proof of the injectivity half of the anabelian Hom-conjecture. The aim is to show that two morphisms f, g : X → Y with the same outer π1-map are equal.

Structural role. The previous page stated a corollary: f = g is concluded under hypotheses on fundamental groups. The most general is (d): the image of π1(X) in π1(Y) has trivial centralizer. Case (c), Y an anabelian elementary Artin curve with open image, is shown to be a special case of (d). Case (d) is reduced to case (e), where moreover π1(X) has trivial centre, by replacing X with an Artin covering. The crossed-out top paragraph records this reduction ('OPS de plus que π1(X) a un centre trivial'). It also notes that one may work with the full profinite (or prime-to-p) fundamental groups rather than their ℓ-adic localizations.

The uncrossed text (§14) reduces the geometric statement over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0 to an arithmetic statement over a finitely generated field.
(1) X, Y, f, g are of finite type, so they descend to a subfield K ⊂ k of finite type over Q. Let K̄ be the algebraic closure of K in k, and let X̄, Ȳ, f̄, ḡ be the base changes to K̄. In characteristic 0, π1 is invariant under extension of algebraically closed base field. Hence π1(f̄) = π1(ḡ) up to conjugation, condition (d) holds for them, and π1(X̄) has trivial centre.
(2) Key group-theoretic point. Let 1 → G → E → Γ → 1 be an extension with Z(G) = 1. Then E ≅ Aut(G) ×_{Out(G)} Γ, so E is determined by the outer action Γ → Out(G). Moreover, a homomorphism of extensions lifting a given φ : G → H is unique when the centralizer of φ(G) in H is trivial. Indeed, two lifts differ elementwise by elements centralizing φ(G).
(3) Apply this to the arithmetic fundamental groups E_{X/K} = π1(X) and E_{Y/K} = π1(Y), which are extensions of Gal(K̄/K) by π1(X̄), resp. π1(Ȳ). Then E_{X/K}, E_{Y/K}, π1(f) and π1(g) are reconstructible from π1(X̄), π1(Ȳ), π1(f̄), π1(ḡ) and the outer Galois actions. Consequently π1(f) = π1(g) (outer) over K.
(4) The page ends with 'On va montrer maintenant la' (we shall now show the). The next page continues with Corollary 3: Y is of finite type over a field K finitely generated over Q, and Y embeds into a torsor under an abelian variety. If π1(f) and π1(g) are conjugate as morphisms of extensions, then f = g. Grothendieck adds that equality of the pushed-out extensions by the abelianizations π1(X̄)^ab, π1(Ȳ)^ab should suffice. Behind this, presumably, is a Kummer-class argument: injectivity of the profinite Kummer map A(L) → H^1(L, T(A)) for finitely generated L, by Mordell–Weil–Lang–Néron.
Applying Corollary 3 then gives f = g over K, hence over k.
errors: The transcription '$\pi_1(\bar f) \neq \pi_1(\bar g)$' must be '=' (outer equality). The argument assumes the geometric maps coincide and deduces equality of the arithmetic ones.
Gap (minor, implicit): reconstructing E_{Y/K} needs Z(π1(Ȳ)) = 1. This follows from (d), since the centre lies in the centralizer of the image.
Gap (minor, implicit): the reduction uses that π1 of varieties in characteristic 0 does not change under extension K̄ ⊂ k of algebraically closed fields. This holds but is not stated.
Gap (minor, implicit): the step uses that f and g descend to the same K. One can always enlarge K, so this is harmless.

ideas.what: Descent of a geometric situation (X, Y, f, g) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 to a field finitely generated over Q, to exploit the Galois action.
ideas.modern_name: Spreading out / reduction to finitely generated base field

ideas.what: An extension of a centre-free group G by Γ is determined by the outer action, E ≅ Aut(G) ×_{Out G} Γ. Lifts of a homomorphism whose image has trivial centralizer are unique.
ideas.modern_name: Centre-free extensions determined by outer action (fibre product with Aut → Out)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical group theory; used systematically in anabelian geometry (Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki)
ideas.where_published: implicit in the letter to Faltings (1983) and the Esquisse; standard in later anabelian literature

ideas.what: Geometric Hom-injectivity (identical outer π1-maps ⇒ f = g) deduced from arithmetic Hom-injectivity over finitely generated fields. The latter holds for targets embedding in torsors under abelian varieties, via abelianized (Kummer) data.
ideas.modern_name: Injectivity part of Grothendieck's anabelian Hom-conjecture; Kummer injectivity via Mordell–Weil
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjecture, 1983 letter to Faltings); Mochizuki 1999 (Hom-form for hyperbolic curves over sub-p-adic fields); injectivity part folklore
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981, circulated, unpublished); letter to Faltings 1983 (formulation of conjectures)

missed.claim: The page shows the geometric injectivity statement 'same outer π1-map ⇒ same morphism' being derived from the arithmetic one over finitely generated fields. The derivation uses only trivial-centralizer conditions to rigidify the extensions. Here the geometric case is treated as a consequence of the arithmetic case rather than the reverse. This is a known mechanism, so it is of documentary interest only.
missed.quote: Mais nos hypothèses impliquent que les extensions $\mathcal{E}_{X/K}$, $\mathcal{E}_{Y/K}$ ... ainsi que les homomorphismes $\pi_1(f)$, $\pi_1(g)$ induits, sont reconstructibles
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical documentation of how Grothendieck organized the injectivity part of the Hom-conjecture in 1981. Mathematically, it is standard today.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine reduction step: descent to a finitely generated field, plus the standard fact that centre-free extensions are determined by outer actions. Its main interest is historical, showing the 1981 architecture of the Hom-injectivity argument. Nothing seems new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: '$\pi_1(\bar{f}) \neq \pi_1(\bar{g})$' should read '$\pi_1(\bar f) = \pi_1(\bar g)$' (the symbol is a hastily written equals sign).
In the crossed-out top paragraph, 'profinis[?]' is likely 'premiers à p' (prime-to-p fundamental groups), contrasted with 'le localisé en ℓ ≠ p'. Reading uncertain.
'(de type fini de $\mathbb{Q}$' should be '(de type fini sur $\mathbb{Q}$)'; the 'de' before Q is struck.
'$\mathcal{E}_{X/K}$ {+$= \pi_1(X)$+}' is correct: the superscript insertions identify the extensions with the arithmetic fundamental groups π1(X), π1(Y) over K.
